messages:
jess: Heads up — during the rotate job at ~12:04 I saw embedding-scoped keys successfully call the /v1/chat/completions route for ~20–30s before failing. Not a public exploit but definitely a scope enforcement gap. anyone around?

marco: logs? request headers?

jess: pasted a tiny snippet: 
```
POST /v1/chat/completions
Authorization: Bearer key-emb-xxXYz
x-scope: embeddings
x-route: /v1/chat/completions
model: redwood-chat-3b
```
response: 200 then 403 after ~30s

anika: that looks like the key's metadata said embeddings, but route allowlist accepted it. we recently changed how we tag keys (route vs model vs scope) — could be a tagging race on rotate.

marco: rotate job flow: 1) create new key; 2) write tags to KMS metadata; 3) publish event to authz-cache to refresh. if step 3 skipped or slow, old cache might have stale allowlist that mismatches new metadata.

infra-bot: deploybot: rotation-job/redwood-rotate-v2 started at 2024-09-11T12:03:45Z (job-id rot-20240911-81).

tony: can we repro locally? create key with embeddings-only, then run rotate path and fire a chat request to see if route check consults KMS or cache first.

jess: repro steps I used: create key via admin UI with scope=embeddings; call embeddings endpoint (ok); trigger rotate from admin (rotate creates new version, re-tags); immediately call chat endpoint -> returned 200; wait ~35s call chat -> 403.

anika: that implies initial calls used cached allowlists that still had legacy wildcard route mapping. After cache TTL expired, the authz service re-evaluated against KMS tags and rejected. so short window where wrong routing allowed.

marco: what's the authz cache TTL? I thought we set it to 15s for tag-sensitive checks.

jess: looks like prod TTL for key->scopes is 60s in authz-cache (see config: AUTHZ_CACHE_TTL=60).

tony: two problems: 1) you can get a transient over-permissive window; 2) rotation audit doesn't correlate event id -> requests so hard to trace affected calls.

sec-bot: security-note: we need rotation event id in the request-level audit logs (e.g., rotation_id or key_version) to link access window to a rotation. filing for compliance review. :warning:

anika: immediate mitigation options: reduce TTL to 1s (risky perf hit), or have rotate job invalidate cache synchronously via pub/sub and block until ack. prefer the latter.

marco: agree. rotate job should publish an explicit invalidation message for the specific key id and wait for authz-cache ack (or at least retry). also add a short grace deny-by-default until tags confirmed?

jess: another note — some downstream route handlers short-circuit authz by consulting route-level allowlist in local memory before calling the central authz api. that means they never saw the invalidation event.

tony: ugh. so we have multiple caches. need a design to ensure rotate invalidation fanout reaches all path caches.

anika: quick plan: (1) rotate job -> publish key-rotation:{key_id}:{new_version} on broker; (2) authz-cache and route-local caches subscribe and ack; (3) rotate job waits up to 5s for N acks (configurable); (4) if acks missing, mark key status=quarantined and halt serving until resolved.

marco: also add audit fields: rotation_job_id, key_version, prev_version in every auth audit log entry for 48h. this makes postmortem and compliance easier.

jess: created draft SE ticket: SE-12473 (rbac: rotation invalidation fanout + audit metadata). I've added the repro steps and log snippets.

infra-bot: ticket created: SE-12473 assigned to @anika with label p0 and security-review required.

tony: for immediate prod safety: roll a hotfix to have route handlers call central authz-check for any key that has rotate_recent=true in KMS metadata (cheap check) until full fanout is in.

anika: agree, will PR the rotate->pubsub ack flow and the audit fields. will also add unit test to simulate multiple caches.

jess: one more ask for audit/compliance: can we backfill affected request ids between rotate start and quiesce? sec-bot mentioned it's needed for customers who ask for timeline.

sec-bot: advice: backfill possible if logs contain key_version or rotation_event in that window. since we didn't have that, we'll approximate by correlating request timestamps + key id and rotation job id. note that may miss some internal retries. recommend we add rotation id to future logs.

marco: noted. i'll add a short runbook for on-call: if rotate job sees ack failures, run a query to list requests with key_id in window and mark them in incident doc.

jess: thanks everyone. tagging @oncall for visibility. i'll follow up in SE-12473 with timeline and proposed PRs. :thumbsup:
